title: The canonical morphism Spec O_{Y,y} -> Y is flat and identifies local rings
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $y\in Y$, $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ its local ring [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with closed point $y'=\mathfrak m$. The *canonical morphism* $c:Y'\to Y$ is the morphism of schemes corresponding to the identity map $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to A$: for any affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Y$ containing $y$, with $y$ the prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, the natural map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is an isomorphism and $c$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R_{\mathfrak p})\to\operatorname{Spec}R=V\subseteq Y$, independent of $V$. Then: (1) $c(y')=y$, and the image $c(Y')$ is the set of generalizations of $y$; in particular $c(Y')\subseteq V$ for every open $V\ni y$, i.e. $c^{-1}(V)=Y'$. (2) For every $q\in Y'$ the local homomorphism $c^\sharp_q:\mathcal O_{Y,c(q)}\to\mathcal O_{Y',q}$ is an isomorphism; for $q=y'$ it is the identity of $A$ under $\mathcal O_{Y',y'}=A_{\mathfrak m}=A$. (3) Consequently $c$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. (4) For every $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal G$ with pullback $c^*\mathcal G$ [def-pc-module-pullback], the map $\mathcal G_y\to(c^*\mathcal G)_{y'}$ sending the germ of $s\in\mathcal G(V)$ to the germ at $y'$ of the image of $s$ under the unit $\mathcal G\to c_*c^*\mathcal G$ (a section of $c^*\mathcal G$ over $c^{-1}(V)=Y'$) is an isomorphism of $A$-modules (the stalk $(c^*\mathcal G)_{y'}$ is $\mathcal G_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\mathcal O_{Y',y'}$ and $c^\sharp_{y'}$ is the identity). (5) For every ideal $J\subseteq A$, the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)\to Y$ induced by $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to A/J$ is $c$ composed with the closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)\to Y'$ given by the quotient map.
